Let’s be completely clear about what is happening here. While the apologists for the ruling establishment try to cry about "stability" and "order," working people and marginalized communities are once again seeing their fundamental democratic rights trampled by those desperately clinging to power. 

Former Zengeza West legislator Job Sikhala had to step up and hold a press conference simply to call for the rejection of proposed constitutional amendments designed to extend President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term of office to 2030. This isn't about "agitators stirring up instability"—that is just the standard authoritarian playbook used to demonize anyone who dares challenge systemic inequality and the erosion of institutional checks and balances. 

The real threat to social cohesion isn't the grassroots resistance or political dissent; it is the entrenchment of a ruling elite determined to bypass the will of the people to protect their own interests. When governance is reduced to safeguarding the unchecked power of a select few at the expense of the working class, fighting back isn't "grandstanding"—it is an essential defense of human rights and democratic accountability. We must stand firm against this authoritarian continuity.
